artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $w$ be an infinite word over a finite alphabet $A$, and let $p_w(n)$ denote its factor complexity, i.e. the number of distinct factors (contiguous finite subwords) of $w$ of length $n$. Suppose that $w$ belongs to a class $\mathcal{C}$ of infinite words characterized by some prescribed asymptotic or combinatorial behavior of the ratio $p_w(n)/n$ (for instance, words with bounded ratio $p_w(n)/n$, or those for which $p_w(n)/n$ converges, etc.).

Recall that an $S$-adic representation of an infinite word $w$ consists of a finite set $S = \{\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_k\}$ of substitutions $\sigma_i : B_i^* \to B_{i-1}^*$ between finite alphabets, together with an infinite directive sequence $(i_n)_{n\ge 1}$ specifying which substitution is applied at each step, such that
$$w = \lim_{n\to\infty} \sigma_{i_1}\sigma_{i_2}\cdots\sigma_{i_n}(a_n)$$
for suitable letters $a_n$. One may further constrain the admissible directive sequences by combinatorial rules (e.g. encoded by a labeled graph or a sofic shift on the index set) governing how the substitutions in $S$ may be composed.

Problem. Provide a characterization of the class $\mathcal{C}$ in terms of an $S$-adic representation: exhibit a finite set $S$ of substitutions, together with explicit rules governing the admissible compositions of elements of $S$, such that an infinite word $w$ belongs to $\mathcal{C}$ if and only if $w$ admits an $S$-adic representation respecting these rules.
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem of giving an S-adic characterization of infinite words/subshifts via the growth rate of factor complexity p(n)/n is the well-known S-adic conjecture, which remains open in full generality. Partial results exist: e.g., an S-adic characterization of minimal subshifts with first difference of complexity satisfying 1 ≤ p(n+1) − p(n) ≤ 2, and improvements of the S-adic conjecture have been obtained, but a complete characterization has not been established.

status_evidence.title: An S-adic characterization of minimal subshifts with first difference of complexity 1 ≤ p(n+1)-p(n) ≤ 2
status_evidence.snippet: Provides an S-adic characterization for a restricted complexity class, indicating the broader problem is partially addressed.
status_evidence.claim: Partial S-adic characterizations exist for restricted complexity regimes.

status_evidence.title: Some improvements of the S-adic conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: The S-adic conjecture postulates the existence of a condition C such that a sequence has linear complexity if and only if it is an S-adic sequence satisfying C for some finite set S of morphisms.
status_evidence.claim: The general S-adic conjecture remains open.

status_evidence.title: Beyond substitutive dynamical systems: S-adic expansions
status_evidence.snippet: Survey on S-adic expansions and their relation to complexity.
status_evidence.claim: S-adic theory is an active area, with the linear-complexity characterization still a guiding open problem.
